title: Why AI Can't Replace Sr Devs
transcript: This engineer got fired and his first move was to record a 40-minute YouTube video. Instead of disappearing completely, he decided to document everything. In this video, [music] he walked through the entire load balancing architecture that he built from scratch, the Envoy proxy system, and the edge infrastructure serving millions of developers. And then, he said something that had nothing to do with code. Building software is easy, but keeping it changeable over the years is the hardest part. He said why build coded AI apps will create maintenance problems nobody is prepared for. >> [music] >> He said the engineers who will survive the AI wave are not the ones who write the most code. They are the ones who understand why the system works at all. That is [music] 8 years of hard-earned clarity sitting in one YouTube video. Here's what I feel. Vasilios will definitely get another job because what he knows does not go out of date. AI might automate the top layer, but the foundation underneath stays exactly the same. The engineers who know why systems work will always be the ones [music] on top. Comment hackernomics and I will send you his video.
